overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by discussing non-executive-session topics (Police policy and legal obligations), holding part of an employee discussion in closed session without notice, and citing the wrong statute.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed individuals in executive sessions on July 25 and August 8 without giving them written notice and an opportunity to be present.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding those portions of the discussion in executive session.

allegations.summary: The Board cited G.L. c. 214, §1B (privacy) to enter executive session rather than the CORI statute, and failed to comply with procedural requirements for convening in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law because it failed to cite to a proper statute to justify its executive session discussion under Purpose 7.

allegations.summary: Much of the executive session discussion concerned Police Department policies, procedures and the Town's legal obligations, which the AG found were not proper executive session topics.

remedy: Release to the public the portion of the July 25 and August 8 executive session minutes concerning Police Department policies and procedures, without redaction or withholding.
Provide the affected employee with an unredacted version of the portion of the minutes concerning that employee within 30 days of receipt of the determination.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: As a result of our finding, we order the Board to release to the public the portion of the executive session minutes concerning the Police Department's policies and procedures.
